scope: Recovery drafts written by the service without a browser: the API process drafts unsaved work on its own schedule, at a normal stop, and retries failures, whether or not any client calls autosave. Storage and recovery only; no chemistry or external formats.
environment: Linux 6.6 (WSL2), Rust 1.95.0, Node 22.22.2; browser checks with Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright build v1194) via playwright-core 1.56.1
design: Each session keeps a DraftSchedule: a draft is due 2 s after the last change it does not hold, and at most 10 s after the first such change, so continuous editing cannot postpone it. A failure is retried after 2, 5, 15, then every 30 s; edits do not push a retry back, and session.draft_failure ({ attempts, retry_in_ms, message }, added within v1 and optional for clients) reports it until a draft succeeds. A background thread in the API process (DraftWriter) checks every 250 ms and writes due drafts through the same path as client autosaves, so it follows #19's request order: it takes the document's turn (at most 3 s; a busy turn is kept as a failed attempt and retried), and one revision is drafted once whoever comes first. A save or a discarding close settles the schedule; an earlier session's draft or another process's draft is never written over (recovery_pending / draft_in_use, retried). On SIGTERM or Ctrl+C the server stops taking requests, the writer stops, and every session with undrafted work is drafted before exit; failures are logged. The CLI commits every edit and has no sessions to draft.

checks.contract_smoke: Passes with real API and CLI processes: an edit over HTTP with no autosave call is drafted within the quiet period and survives SIGKILL (recovered exactly, with its undo history); SIGTERM drafts the last edit before exit; continuous edits are drafted no earlier than about 9.5 s and within 13 s; with drafts/ read-only the failure is reported in session.draft_failure and the draft is written on the next retry once the permission is back, clearing the failure. The earlier storage-feedback, document-list, and recovery steps still pass with the writer running.

limits: Without the web page, up to about 10 seconds of editing (plus the 250 ms check and the write) is lost in a crash; longer while drafting fails or an earlier draft blocks it.

Drafting writes while holding the process's session table, as client autosaves already did, so a stalled disk delays other requests for that long; the background writer also waits up to 3 s per document whose turn is held, so a stalled save delays other documents' drafts in that pass.
At a normal stop, each session with undrafted work is drafted in turn; a document whose turn stays busy adds up to 3 s to the stop.
The web page shows its own autosave state; it does not display session.draft_failure, which is for other clients and diagnostics.
Drafts never expire and are never cleaned up automatically.
independent_review: A reviewer without this session's context read bdd6ce6: no P1 or P2. P3: the background writer could open again a session closed while it waited for another document's turn; the schedule was updated after the turn and lock were released, so a success could keep a stale failure and a busy autosave of already-drafted work reported a failure; retries counted from before the turn wait (a busy failure was retried on the next tick); the contract's 10-second guarantee did not mention that a busy document delays the others; two test assertions could not fail; a server error skipped drafting at the stop. All fixed: the service drafts only open sessions, the schedule moves under the session lock with the write, failures count from when they happen, the guarantee states the delay, and the stop drafts even after a server error.
